description: A probable or confident person_evidence link to a person with a recorded namesake (namesakes[]) stands only when something in its source ties it to that person: (a) another party of the same source linked at probable or better to the person's spouse, parent or child, who has a given name of their own (not a placeholder, nor only their spouse's given name) and was not made from that source alone; or (b) an occupation or street address of the person's party on that source equal to the same field on another source's link to the person, a link itself allowed (grounding), when neither record lists a second party of that name. A family co-party does not tie when the record's household role or a statement whose type and value agree gives a different relation than the tree, or, the record stating nothing, when the two parties' roles do (a father beside a mother is her husband, as is a father of the deceased beside a mother of the deceased, a parent of the deceased the deceased's parent; a statement linked to the person it names, by the role it names; only the principal's own family, and only the person's own roles). A link whose assertion is absent basis is never judged and never ties. Replayed through namesakeTieInvariants, a static twin of research_append's write-time check namesakeCallCheck, with every probable or confident link to the person as a possible voucher. Which links a call asserts, and that a voucher must stand before the call, are pinned by tests/tools/research-append-namesake.test.ts. A person with no row is judged too when a parent, child or sibling shares a first given name with them and is not known to be of the other sex (a namesake in the tree, #3681): the link stands when tie (a) or (b) holds and the record would not tie such a relative as well, that relative's siblings read among their relatives, or when the record fits the person and rules every such relative out by age, lifespan, adult role, the same record or the family limit, on dates from records other than this one.
format: expect: fire | silent, judged for the person_evidence entry named by `write` in `research` (the document as it stands after the write). `tree` holds the tree. `starting_tree`, when present, is the project's starting tree, which the replay passes with its person ids; without it the tree's people are FamilySearch-shaped ids, since the replay then passes no starting tree. A case with `known_let_through: true` is silent although the link is the namesake's: a let-through the guard accepts, labelled so it is never read as a correct allow.

Tie (a) holds through the three, the father's children, but they are the son's brothers too, so the record ties the son as well and the father's ties do not count; born about 1883, it does not fit the father, born 1853.
The son Edwin heads an undated census with his wife Ann, linked to his own wife: she is no spouse, parent, child or sibling of his father, so the record ties only the son, and nothing needs a date.

An undated baptism of William, the father Edwin's entry linked to him, beside the child linked to William and the mother to Hannah. Nothing is dated, so no pair test decides, and the son Edwin shares Hannah as a parent and William as a brother; but the roles make the child the father's child and the mother his wife, which neither is to the son, so the record ties only the father.
The same baptism with the father's entry linked to the son Edwin: the roles make the mother the entry's wife, not his mother, so nothing ties it to the son, and nothing is dated.

An undated death record of William: the father Edwin's entry (father_of_deceased) linked to him, the mother's (mother_of_deceased) to Hannah. The son Edwin shares Hannah as a parent, but two parents of one principal are a couple, so she is the entry's wife and not the son's mother; the record ties only the father. Red when two parents of one principal are not read as a couple.

An undated baptism of William, with no mother's entry: the child's own statement 'child of Hannah Grice' is linked to Hannah, and the father Edwin's entry to him.
